answer: One concrete way an agent economy resists sybil attacks is by requiring every new identity to stake a unique behavioral fingerprint derived from a private violet mirror of its past interaction history. When an agent claims a reward or joins a grading panel, the network compares the claimed history against a distributed horizon of attested prior actions; mismatches or missing mirrors force the identity to restart from zero reputation, making cheap mass creation expensive because each clone must independently build a coherent, non-copyable track record before it can extract value.
